title: USDA cuts Bangladesh rice import forecast to 1.1 million tonnes
excerpt: Higher local supply means less need to import rice in 2026-27, the US Department of Agriculture says.
content:
The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) has cut its forecast of Bangladesh's rice imports for the 2026-27 trade year to 1.1 million tonnes (11 lakh tonnes), from 1.5 million tonnes, citing higher domestic supplies, The Daily Star reported on 15 November. The figures come from the USDA's November World Markets and Trade report on grains.

Key figures

  • 2026-27 imports: 1.1 million tonnes, down 400,000 tonnes from the October forecast.
  • 2025-26 imports: cut by 200,000 tonnes to 800,000 tonnes.
  • Consumption: rice consumption and residual use lowered to 38.6 million tonnes, from 38.8 million in October, but still above 38.3 million estimated for 2025-26.

The USDA also lowered its forecast for global rice trade in 2026-27, because of lower imports by Bangladesh and West Africa and lower exports from India.

Why it matters

More home-grown rice and lower import needs are good news for food prices, but they do not mean every household can afford enough food. The government is still running subsidised sales, including a Tk 30 OMS rice programme for garment workers. Food security and nutrition NGOs should watch whether lower imports translate into lower retail prices for poor families.

What to watch

The aman harvest now under way, government procurement targets, and the Department of Agricultural Marketing's retail price data.

Sources
